name: Vespid Dynamics Toxin Dart Rifle TDR-3 'Asp'
description: A suppressed pneumatic rifle firing hollow-point darts loaded with selectable toxin payloads. The TDR-3 operates on compressed gas propulsion, producing no muzzle flash and minimal acoustic signature — the loudest component is the dart's impact. Vespid supplies a range of toxin capsules from incapacitant to lethal, color-coded and loaded into the dart's reservoir chamber before firing. The weapon has become the preferred tool of corporate assassination teams who need deniable, quiet elimination at medium range.
specifications:
propulsion: Compressed nitrogen, 180 m/s dart velocity
effective range: 15-80 meters
magazine: 5-dart rotary chamber
acoustic signature: 38 dB at 1 meter
toxin options: Incapacitant (blue), paralytic (yellow), lethal (red), tracer compound (green)
weight: 2.8 kg with optic
optics: Integrated 4x thermal with wind compensation
story_hooks: A series of apparently natural deaths among mid-tier corporate managers has been linked by a single commonality — trace compounds consistent with TDR-3 green tracer darts found in their bloodwork.
A Vespid insider is selling a new toxin capsule on the black market that induces permanent memory loss of the preceding 72 hours — perfect for witnesses.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, predatory rifle with a distinctly organic aesthetic — the body curves like a serpent's spine, tapering toward a slim muzzle. The overall silhouette is compact and purposeful, built for close-quarters precision work rather than distance engagement. Its pneumatic engineering gives it an almost medical appearance, clinical and sterile.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length 94 cm, barrel 38 cm, stock-to-trigger 32 cm. Compact enough for one-handed support, long enough for accurate targeting.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and light in hand — 2.8 kg feels almost insubstantial, the weight distributed evenly along the frame. Designed for extended surveillance work where fatigue is a liability.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite body with aerospace-grade polymer chassis. The barrel assembly is reinforced steel with internal hardening for precision dart acceleration.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte black with a subtle iridescent sheen visible only under direct light — a coating that minimizes glint. Wear reveals dark graphite beneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary black (99% of visible surface), accent trim in brushed gunmetal gray along the rail system. The rotary toxin chamber visible through reinforced polymer housing shows color-coded dart tips: blue, yellow, red, green.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with aggressive micro-texturing for gloved operation. The foregrip features shallow ridges designed for thumb-over-bore positioning.
distinctive_features: Integrated 4x thermal optic mounted flush to the upper receiver — no glass glint, fully digital readout
Rotary 5-dart toxin chamber visible from the side, color-coded payloads backlit by faint LED indicator ring
Curved, serpentine rail system suggesting the weapon's 'Asp' designation
Ultra-slim suppressor integrated into the barrel assembly — appears as a subtle tapered extension
Pressure gauge (analog needle, barely 2cm wide) set into the stock junction
Manual selector lever with three positions: SAFE, SINGLE, RAPID (pneumatic pulse mode)
Faint engraving of a coiled viper striking downward along the receiver
Wear patterns on the grip and cheek rest consistent with daily tactical use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS stamped in clean sans-serif lettering just above the trigger guard. Beneath that, small text: TDR-3 / ASP / PNEUMATIC TOXIN DELIVERY. A small holographic serial plate mounted on the left side of the receiver, iridescent blue when tilted.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Micro-scratches in the polymer, faint carbon residue around the dart chamber, a thin layer of synthetic oil on the rail system. The thermal optic shows signs of dust exposure despite protective lens coating. This is a tool actively in use, not a showpiece.
